label: Complex Manifolds
notes: Lecture 15 spans printed pages 81 through 87. We graduate from the pointwise linear algebra of Lecture 14 to genuine complex manifolds, glued from charts whose transition maps are biholomorphic. The goal is to see how holomorphic gluing upgrades an almost complex structure into an integrable one.

label: Holomorphic Atlas
notes: A complex manifold of dimension n carries charts into open sets of complex n-space, with all transition maps biholomorphic. Emphasize that the requirement is genuinely stronger than smoothness: each transition and its inverse must satisfy the Cauchy-Riemann equations, so they are holomorphic in every variable simultaneously.

label: The Induced J
notes: Each holomorphic chart carries the standard rotation that sends the x partials to the y partials. Because transition maps are holomorphic, their differentials commute with this rotation, so the local definitions agree on overlaps. The result is a globally well-defined almost complex structure J squaring to minus the identity.

label: Type Decomposition
notes: Complexifying the tangent bundle and diagonalizing J splits it into the plus-i eigenspace and the minus-i eigenspace, the holomorphic and antiholomorphic tangents. Dually the one-forms split into dz and dz-bar pieces, and k-forms refine into bidegree types counting holomorphic versus antiholomorphic factors.

label: Partial and Dbar
notes: On a complex manifold the exterior derivative splits cleanly as partial plus dbar, raising holomorphic and antiholomorphic degree respectively. This is exactly where integrability matters: the splitting closes only because holomorphic coordinates exist. From d squared equals zero we extract the crucial relation dbar squared equals zero.

label: Integrability
notes: An abstract almost complex structure need not come from any atlas. Integrability is precisely the condition that holomorphic coordinates exist locally. Walk students through the chain: complex charts give a closed type splitting, which forces the bracket of two holomorphic vector fields to stay holomorphic, the Frobenius-style obstruction.

label: Nijenhuis Tensor
notes: The Nijenhuis tensor measures the failure of the holomorphic tangent distribution to be involutive. It is a genuine tensor, built from brackets of J-twisted vector fields, vanishing automatically in real dimension two. Stress that it is computable pointwise, turning integrability into an algebraic condition on J and its first derivatives.

label: Newlander-Nirenberg
notes: The Newlander-Nirenberg theorem is the deep payoff: an almost complex structure is integrable, hence arises from a genuine complex atlas, if and only if its Nijenhuis tensor vanishes, equivalently dbar squared equals zero. This converts a hard PDE existence problem into a finite algebraic test on J.

label: Holomorphic Objects
notes: With integrability secured, holomorphic functions, forms, and vector bundles all make invariant sense. A function is holomorphic when dbar kills it; transition functions of a holomorphic bundle are holomorphic matrix-valued maps. The dbar operator then organizes these objects into the Dolbeault complex and its cohomology.

label: Examples
notes: Survey the canonical examples: complex n-space itself, complex tori as quotients by a lattice, and complex projective space with its homogeneous coordinates. These are the manifolds we return to when building Kahler geometry, so anchoring the definitions in them now pays off in the lectures ahead.

label: CP^n Charts
notes: Complex projective space is the workhorse example. Homogeneous coordinates define standard affine charts by dividing by a nonzero coordinate. On overlaps the transition maps are holomorphic, the model being w equals one over z on the projective line, holomorphic away from the excluded point. Projective varieties inherit this structure.

label: Recap
notes: Recap the logical spine: holomorphic atlases induce a canonical J, the type splitting and dbar operator follow, and Newlander-Nirenberg pins integrability to the vanishing Nijenhuis tensor. Preview that adding a compatible symplectic form to this complex structure produces the Kahler manifolds of the coming lectures.
